subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a two's complement number, the most significant bit:
options: Always represents a positive power of two
questions.explain: In two's complement the MSB carries a negative weight (e.g. -128 in 8 bits), which is why it indicates sign.

questions.q: How many distinct characters can the standard 7-bit ASCII code represent?
questions.explain: 7 bits give 2^7 = 128 distinct codes.

questions.q: In a singly linked list, each node typically stores:
options: A pointer to the previous node only
Data and a pointer to the next node
questions.explain: A singly linked list node holds its data and a pointer (reference) to the next node in the list.

questions.q: What is the 8-bit two's complement representation of -20?
In a circular queue, what advantage does it have over a simple linear queue using an array?
options: It reuses freed space at the front by wrapping the rear pointer around
It removes the need for a front pointer
questions.explain: A circular queue wraps the rear pointer to the start, reusing slots vacated by dequeued items.

questions.q: A binary tree node may have at most how many children?
questions.explain: By definition each node of a binary tree has at most two children (left and right).

questions.q: In a doubly linked list, each node differs from a singly linked list node by also storing:
options: A pointer to the previous node
questions.explain: A doubly linked list node holds pointers to both the next and the previous nodes, allowing two-way traversal.

questions.q: Applying a bitwise AND with the mask 00001111 to a byte will:
options: Set the upper four bits and clear the lower four
Shift the bits left by four
Clear (zero) the upper four bits and keep the lower four
questions.explain: AND with 00001111 keeps the lower nibble unchanged and forces the upper nibble to 0.

questions.q: Why is a stack described as the structure that enables backtracking, such as the 'undo' feature?
options: Because the most recent action is on top and is the first to be reversed
Because it uses a hash function
Because it serves items in arrival order
questions.explain: A stack's LIFO behaviour means the last action performed is the first one undone.

questions.q: In a 2D array declared as A[rows][columns], element A[2][3] refers to:
options: The element at row index 2, column index 3
questions.explain: A 2D array is indexed by row then column, so A[2][3] is the cell at row 2, column 3.

questions.q: A queue is the most appropriate structure for which of the following uses?
options: Buffering data such as a print job spooler
questions.explain: A FIFO queue suits buffering, where items are processed in the order they arrive, e.g. a print spooler.

questions.q: A stack is an abstract data type that operates on which principle?
questions.explain: A stack is LIFO: the most recently pushed item is the first one popped.

questions.q: The Vernam cipher (one-time pad) is theoretically unbreakable provided the key is:
options: A simple shift of three letters
Truly random, at least as long as the message, used only once and kept secret
Shorter than the message and reused
questions.explain: A Vernam cipher is perfectly secure only with a truly random key as long as the message, used once and kept secret.

questions.q: To insert a new node between two existing nodes in a linked list, you must:
options: Update the pointers so the previous node points to the new node and the new node points to the following node
Shift all subsequent elements one place along
Recompute a hash for every node
questions.explain: Insertion in a linked list only requires repointing the surrounding nodes' pointers, no shifting of elements.

questions.q: The Nyquist theorem states that to accurately reconstruct a signal, the sampling rate must be at least:
options: Twice the highest frequency present in the signal
Equal to the highest frequency present
questions.explain: Nyquist requires sampling at a minimum of twice the highest frequency component to avoid aliasing.

questions.q: A post-order traversal of a binary tree visits nodes in which order?
questions.explain: Post-order visits the left subtree, then the right subtree, then the root last.

questions.q: Run-length encoding (RLE) is most effective when data contains:
options: Highly random data with no repetition
Many long runs of repeated identical values
questions.explain: RLE replaces consecutive repeated values with a count and value, so it works best on long runs.

questions.q: A pre-order traversal of a binary tree visits nodes in which order?
questions.explain: Pre-order visits the root first, then the left subtree, then the right subtree.

questions.q: In asymmetric (public-key) encryption, a message encrypted with a recipient's public key can be decrypted using:
questions.explain: Data encrypted with the public key can only be decrypted with the matching private key.

questions.q: For a fixed total word length, increasing the number of mantissa bits (at the expense of exponent bits) will:
questions.explain: More mantissa bits give greater precision, but fewer exponent bits reduce the available range.

questions.q: Floating-point underflow occurs when a number is:
options: Too small in magnitude (too close to zero) to be represented
Too large in magnitude to store
questions.explain: Underflow happens when a value is too small in magnitude for the exponent range to represent.

questions.q: Which data structure is used internally to manage the sequence of subroutine calls and returns (recursion)?
questions.explain: The call stack stores return addresses and local data for each active subroutine call in LIFO order.

questions.q: Attempting to pop from an empty stack causes which condition?
questions.explain: Removing from an empty stack is a stack underflow; adding beyond capacity is overflow.

questions.q: A key advantage of Unicode (e.g. UTF-8/UTF-16) over ASCII is that it:
options: Can represent characters from a vast range of languages and symbols
Stores numbers more efficiently than binary
Uses fewer bits per character in all cases
Cannot represent the original ASCII characters
questions.explain: Unicode provides code points for characters across the world's writing systems, far beyond ASCII's set.

questions.q: Which statement about lossless compression is correct?
options: It always achieves higher ratios than lossy compression
Some original data is permanently discarded
The original data can be perfectly reconstructed from the compressed file
It can only be used on text files
questions.explain: Lossless compression allows exact reconstruction of the original data with no information lost.

questions.q: Increasing the bit depth (resolution) of audio sampling improves:
options: The number of samples per second
The accuracy of each recorded amplitude value
questions.explain: More bits per sample give finer amplitude resolution, more accurately representing each sample.

questions.q: In floating-point representation, the exponent primarily determines:
questions.explain: The exponent scales the mantissa and so governs the range/magnitude of values that can be represented.

questions.q: In a binary search tree, for any given node, values in its left subtree are:
questions.explain: In a BST, the left subtree contains values less than the node and the right subtree values greater.

questions.q: Which statement about an array is true compared with a linked list?
options: An array allows direct (random) indexed access to any element in constant time
An array is always dynamic in size
An array can only be traversed via pointers
questions.explain: Arrays support O(1) random access by index, whereas a linked list must be traversed sequentially.

questions.q: Which data structure is most naturally used to evaluate a reverse Polish (postfix) expression?
questions.explain: A stack handles postfix evaluation by pushing operands and popping them when an operator is met.
